1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 Bg7 4.e4 O-O {Most of the time this transposes to 
the slightly more popular ...d6, but on occasion White opts for the added 
option of an aggressive space grab.} ( 4...d6 ) 5.e5 $6 {I can't recommend
this move, but it's not objectively so bad. In my opinion, the onus is now
on White to justify this play though.} 5...Ne8 6.f4 ( 6.h4 $13 {An 
interesting option that has been tried a few times. It might be worth a 
punt and is in the mold of h4 lines against the Gruenfeld.} ) ( 6.Be3 $13 
{This is a bit safer, but ...d6 will chip away at the center and e5 $6 
remains suspect.} ) 6...d6 {An early e5 almost always invites ...d6, 
exchanging the pawn and questioning White's advance.} 7.Be3 c5 $1 {Already
on move 7, the center is collapsing.} 8.dxc5 Nc6 9.cxd6 exd6 10.Ne4 $2 {
This is really too much and begs punishment. White has developed only two 
pieces by move 10, and now he moves one again. It is only too natural for 
Black to be able to offer material to attack here.} ( 10.Nf3 $12 {Fortune 
favors the cautious, and White's position is still tenable here though I 
think most would prefer Black.} ) 10...Bf5 $1 {Of course, Fischer does not
defend d6, but develops again.} 11.Ng3 ( 11.Nxd6 Nxd6 12.Qxd6 Qe8 $17 {
preparing ...d6 and ...Rd8 is very strong. Black's attack against the 
uncastled White king is likely a winning one.} ( 12...Qxd6 13.exd6 Nb4 $15
{This is also dangerous and feels like a line Fischer might have pursued.}
) ) 11...Be6 12.Nf3 Qc7 {Pressure is added to e5 while Rd8 is prepared and
a queen trade is avoided.} 13.Qb1 $6 {Preparing the following move which 
desperately tries to close the center. I very much dislike this move which
sidelines the queen and doesn't develop, but I have no better suggestions 
either.} 13...dxe5 14.f5 e4 $5 ( 14...gxf5 15.Nxf5 Bxf5 16.Qxf5 Nd6 {With 
...e4 and ...f5 in the works is objectively very powerful and is 
Stockfish's preference. Fischer's line avoids moving his g-pawn and 
weakening his light squares which might give White hints of counterplay.} 
) 15.fxe6 $2 ( 15.Qxe4 {White must try this. It's very scary, but all else
loses by force.} 15...Bxb2 $17 ) 15...exf3 16.gxf3 f5 $1 {The e6-pawn is 
left alive only briefly. When it falls, e-file devestation ensues. Black's
pieces now surge forward with every move through to the game's end.} 17.f4
{...f4 had to be stopped.} 17...Nf6 18.Be2 Rfe8 $1 {It is time for the 
rooks to enter the play.} 19.Kf2 Rxe6 20.Re1 Rae8 $1 {My students could 
learn so much from the way Fischer has included all of his pieces in the 
attack here. In my experience, the rooks are too often left excluded while
attacking players continue to make threats with their minor pieces.} 21.
